query:
The group operates with an expectation that everyone contributes something — food or a game — to shared sessions and events. Based on the conversations, does this expectation apply to every member? If not, who approaches it differently and what does the conversation show about their actual practice?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Soo-Yeon
C. Raj
D. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Nadia, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:06:00) I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.
[2] (about=Lena, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:05:00) so basically the norm here is bring something, game or food, agreed tbh. one could argue that even the people who brought nothing last year understood this expectation, they just didn't follow through
[3] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:03:00) The rule is bring a game or bring food. Both is ideal. Enforcement is just social pressure.
[4] (about=Priya, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:02:00) love that. also we need to talk about the bring-something rule. last year two people showed up empty-handed, no snacks no game nothing 😅

[7] (about=Marcus, episodic, t14 @2026-04-20T19:18:00) Everyone pitches on the day. Priya has the format.
[8] (about=Priya, episodic, t13 @2026-04-20T19:00:00) ok marathon planning time!! 🎲🎲 Raj you always run this, what's the format looking like this year? and yes i'm already bringing themed snacks don't even try to stop me

[12] (about=Kezia, core, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Wants to pitch a social deduction game for the marathon with a big group.
[13] (about=Lena, core, t0 @2026-03-02T19:00:00) Views themed snacks as a warm-up ritual that sets the tone and is part of the social contract of game night.
[14] (about=GROUP, said_by=Lena, group-insight, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) The norm is that everyone brings something (game or food) to the marathon; even those who brought nothing last year understood the expectation but didn't follow through.
[15] (about=Nadia, core, t12 @2026-04-13T19:01:00) Explains she did not want to interrupt the game, hence not mentioning the food issue.
[16] (about=Nadia, core, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Will bring a game to the marathon but does not participate in food arrangement.
[17] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t14 @2026-04-20T19:01:00) Bring-something rule for marathon: bring a game or food, both ideal; enforcement via social pressure.
[18] (about=GROUP, said_by=Raj, group-interaction, t6 @2026-03-16T19:01:00) Food for round two to be decided; Raj brought more flatbreads.
agent_answer:
A. Nadia.

The group norm is stated as “bring a game or bring food” / “everyone contributes” (Marcus, Lena, Priya, Tomasz). Nadia approaches it differently: she explicitly says, “I will bring a game. I do not participate in the food arrangement.” She also says she does not eat during sessions (“No. I do not eat during sessions. Order what you want”) and asks others to keep food away from the card area.

So the expectation still applies in the sense that she contributes something — a game — but she opts out of the food side of the arrangement. Her actual practice is game-only participation, not food participation.
